title: Shimon Kamatria
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2, he asks Rabbi Chiya bar Abba, “Since I am a donkey-driver and go up to Jerusalem every year, must we tear our garments?” He replies, “If,” etc. Afterwards Rabbi Chuna and Shimon Kamatria say in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman that the nun is suspended in “Yehonatan, son of Gershom, son of Menashe.” If he was worthy, he is called son of Moshe, etc.

notes.text: Hyman says every year; the checked Berakhot paragraph has every [time/hour], in a discussion of the30-day interval. The annual/frequent wording difference remains open. The next full paragraph explicitly joins Chuna and Shimon as reporters. The suspended nun makes the difference between Menashe and Moshe.

Both saved whole Venice Berakhot 9:2 scalars were read. The first explicitly says EVERY YEAR and gives the thirty-day answer; the second joins Rabbi Chuna AND Shimon Kamatria in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman's name. This withdraws a blanket annual-versus-frequent mismatch claim for Venice while preserving the earlier other-edition time/hour reading as a separate witness. Hyman has Chiyya bar Abba where Venice has bar Ba. שנקרע is rendered must WE tear, preserving the supplied first-person plural. The worthy condition concerns the named descendant, not Moshe. Both etc. endings remain Hyman's abbreviations; the rest of the named paragraph is not imported into his notice. These exact named title occurrences support full Rabbi without a universal identity binding.

Venice Berakhot 9:2 agrees with Hyman’s “every year.” Guggenheimer reads “every [hour],” rendered “all the time” in his translation and attributed there to the Rome manuscript. Both editions give the thirty-day answer and join Chuna and Shimon as transmitters in Shmuel bar Nachman’s name. Both Hebrew editions have Chiya bar Ba where Hyman has bar Abba. In Judges 18:30 the suspended nun distinguishes Menashe from Moshe. The fuller Yerushalmi applies the condition of merit to the descendant. Hyman abbreviates both quotations.
